content.text: open figma https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2?node-id=636-375 in cluade in browser, and figure out why the 18a - initial mockup seems blurred/covered comppared to other 3 such as 18b - recognized

The 18a mockup looks washed out because the whole "18a — Initial" frame is set to **20% opacity** in Figma. The other frames are at 100%, so the gray page background shows through 18a and makes it look covered.

What I checked in the Add Printer Flow page:
- **"18a — Initial"**: Appearance → Opacity is **20%**. Because it's set on the frame, all three of its layers fade together: `simulated-desktop` (the fake desktop behind the dialog), `scrim` (the dark overlay) and `modal-dialog`.
- **"18b — Recognized"**: Opacity is **100%**. The frame is built from the same three layers, so the frames differ only in opacity.

It's probably an accident. Pressing a number key while a frame is selected sets its opacity (2 gives 20%), so a stray keypress would do it.

**To fix:** select "18a — Initial" and press `0` (which sets 100%), or type 100 in the Opacity field. I haven't changed anything, and the file is still open in your Chrome tab. I can set it for you if you want.

The "18a — Initial" frame in the JusPrin v2 Figma file is now at 100% opacity, and it matches the other three mockups (18b, 18c, 18d). Figma confirmed the change with an "Opacity set to 100%" message, the Opacity field reads 100%, and the frame is no longer faded on the canvas.

Typing 100 into the Opacity field didn't take; it still showed 20%. Selecting the frame and pressing `0`, Figma's shortcut for 100% opacity, worked. Figma saves automatically, so there's nothing else to do, and the file is still open in your Chrome tab.
